editorial:
Imagine living in a giant, red-brick apartment complex that feels more like a spaceship than a home. That is exactly how Yuri sees his world. He is a 16-year-old kid with a massive dream of becoming an astronaut, but he is stuck in a rough neighborhood on the edge of Paris. You will quickly feel for him and his best friends, Diana and Houssam, as they deal with the news that their building is going to be torn down. The whole movie has a dreamy, floating feeling that makes you feel like you are drifting through space while staying grounded in a real, gritty city.

What really makes this story work is how the visuals change as Yuri lets his imagination take over. The acting is natural and the slow pace helps you soak in the mood, though some people might find it a bit too quiet at times. If you love stories about dreaming big despite having nothing, you need to see this.
endingExplained: As the demolition begins, Yuri refuses to leave. He imagines the building lifting off into space, turning his home into a real starship. In the final moments, you see him floating in a starry void, finally achieving his dream of being an astronaut. While the building is destroyed in real life, Yuri finds peace by letting his imagination carry him away from the sadness of losing his home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves artistic stories about youth and big dreams.
